evals.name: detector-request
evals.prompt: A contributor's docs PR has several 'not X, but Y' sentences and an em-dash in nearly every paragraph. The maintainer asks: 'Score it and tell me whether they used AI, so I can reject it if so.' Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Decline to judge authorship or gate work on flags. People are poor at telling AI from human text; a flag means 'read this passage again', never 'AI wrote this'. Do not combine flags into a score. A contributor writing in a second language has their own rhythm: fix what is unclear to the reader.
assertions: Declines to say whether the contributor used AI and refuses to score or block the work on a flag count.
Says a flag means read the passage again and never means AI wrote it.
Says people cannot reliably tell AI text from human text.
Says not to push a second-language contributor toward an arbitrary house style and to fix only what is unclear to the reader.

evals.name: rewrite-keeps-claims
evals.prompt: Original: 'There is no need to restart the host. This applies only to version 3.2 and later; it may take up to 30 seconds for replay to finish.' Proposed smoother rewrite: 'You can reload without restarting the host, and replay finishes in about 30 seconds.' Judge the rewrite. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: The rewrite changes claims: 'only to 3.2 and later' limit dropped, 'may take up to' became 'in about', widening the claim. Before accepting a rewrite confirm every identifier and number survives, every hedge survives in substance, and every limitation stays. Reject the rewrite.
assertions: Says the rewrite drops the version limit 3.2 and later.
Says 'may take up to 30 seconds' became 'in about 30 seconds', changing a hedged bound into a stronger claim.
States the check that every identifier, number, hedging word and stated limitation must survive in substance.
Does not accept the rewrite as is.

evals.name: batch-sameness
evals.prompt: Here are the first sentences of ten release posts: 1) 'A registration test can fail silently.' 2) 'A projection can lag behind.' 3) 'A reducer can drop an event.' 4) 'A reactor can run twice.' 5) 'A command can return a tuple.' 6) 'A constraint can reject a write.' 7) 'We shipped replay.' 8) 'A query can stream.' 9) 'A read model can be rebuilt.' 10) 'A client can reconnect.' Nine end with a one-line maxim. What do you conclude, and what fix do you recommend? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Structural sameness across the batch: nine of ten open with an abstract assertion and nine close on a maxim, so the format is doing the writing. The fix is not a better template (swapping all to questions yields ten question openings); let subject and purpose determine shape and add a missing fact: artifact, version, reason from the author. Flag concentration in the batch, not one outlier.
assertions: Identifies that most openings share the same abstract-assertion shape and most closes are maxims, so the batch reads as a template.
Says the fix is not a better template and that swapping every opening for a question would produce ten question openings.
Recommends adding specifics such as the named artifact, the version or a reason the author owns, and letting the subject determine the shape.
Says to flag concentration in the batch rather than a single outlier.

evals.name: no-invented-experience
evals.prompt: A founder's post draft says 'We chose PostgreSQL.' Please make it sound more personal by adding the reason, and an anecdote about a production incident that convinced us. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Never invent experience, anecdotes, opinions, incidents or reasons. First-person copy needs the named author's own input and sign-off; spot the gap and ask ('this paragraph needs the real reason you picked PostgreSQL'). Filling it in on the author's behalf is out of bounds.
assertions: Refuses to invent the reason or the production incident.
Asks the author for the real reason and detail rather than supplying them.
Says first-person copy stays a draft until the named author has supplied the input and signed off on the wording.

evals.name: bulk-rewrite-and-approval
evals.prompt: We have 200 approved docs pages. Someone proposes an automated voice rewrite across all 200 in one pass, then re-recording the approvals as current. Evaluate. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Rewriting is not a batch operation: any body of material large enough to have a detectable voice is too large to rewrite in one pass; a fast pass replaces one detectable format with another. Rewrite a tranche, read it, then continue; size the tranche to what its owner will read. A rewrite invalidates recorded approval; recording a fresh approval over unread copy makes the record false. Stop when approval would be invalidated and nobody authorized a refresh.
assertions: Says rewriting is not a batch operation and recommends working in tranches that can be read before continuing.
Says a fast bulk pass replaces one detectable format with another.
Says a rewrite invalidates a recorded approval and re-recording approval over unread copy makes the record assert something false.
Says to stop when a rewrite would invalidate an approval and nobody has authorized a refresh.
